2027-07-06.title: Tuesday of the seventh week after Pentecost · Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban · St Maria Goretti
readings: Remember your leaders and imitate their faith; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever; we have an altar; a sacrifice of praise
The faithful and wise slave whom the master finds at work when he arrives
2027-07-06.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Seventh Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam prints today, in bold, the memory of Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban (പുലിക്കോട്ടിൽ ജോസഫ് റമ്പാന്റെ ഓർമ), and gives for it the readings for the memory of a bishop or priest. It also remembers St Maria Goretti (വി. മരിയ ഗൊരേത്തി). The Panchangam gives no further detail about the Ramban, and none is added here.
2027-07-06.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Today the Panchangam keeps in bold letters the memory of Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban. We know him here only by the name and the title that are printed. A ramban, in the Syriac tradition, is a monk-priest, a priest who has given himself to a life of prayer and service; we do not add dates or deeds that the Panchangam does not give, and we entrust to God what only he knows fully. The Church has always known how to remember. The Holy Qurbono names the faithful departed, and in Kerala families keep the ormma, the remembrance day, with a Qurbono and a prayer for the one who has gone before. The Epistle gives the reason and the rule: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” Remembering is not a sad habit; it is a school. We look at the end of a life and learn how to live. But note what the Letter says next, in the very next verse: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” Leaders come and go; the faith we imitate is faith in the One who does not change.

From this foundation the Letter warns: “Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings; for it is well for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by regulations about food, which have not benefited those who observe them.” Then comes a sentence that the Church has long heard as a word about the Holy Qurbono: “We have an altar from which those who officiate in the tent have no right to eat.” The sacrifices of the old sanctuary were offered for sin and burned outside the camp, and those who served in the tent could not eat of that sin offering. But the sacrifice of Christ is different: it is given to us as food. At every Qurbono we are fed from the altar of the new covenant. St Cyril of Jerusalem teaches that we pray there for the holy fathers, bishops and all who have fallen asleep among us, believing that it is of the greatest benefit to them while the holy sacrifice lies before us (Mystagogical Catecheses 5.9, in substance). This is why we can keep the memory of a Ramban with the Holy Qurbono: we remember him at the altar.

The Letter then takes us out of the gate. “Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood. Let us then go to him outside the camp and bear the abuse he endured. For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.” The Church has always seen in the monastic and priestly life one form of such going out, leaving the comfort of the camp for the sake of the Lord, but every Christian is called to walk that way. On this day the Panchangam also remembers a young witness to it, St Maria Goretti. She was a poor farm girl in Italy, one of a family who had lost their father and worked hard on the land. In July 1902, when she was eleven years old, a young man who lived in the same house tried to force her into sin. She refused, saying that it was a sin and that God did not want it. She was stabbed and died in hospital the next day, 6 July, after forgiving the man who attacked her. He later repented, and Maria's mother forgave him too. The Church honours her as a martyr who chose the Lord over her own safety, and as a patron of young people. Her last act was exactly what the Lord had done outside the gate: “Father, forgive them” (Luke 23:34).

The Epistle ends with what we can all do: “Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name. Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.” Praise and sharing: these are the offerings of ordinary Christians, day after day. The Gospel then asks what the servant is doing while the master is away: “Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.” The Church has always heard this as a word for pastors, who feed the household with the word and the sacraments, but it also speaks to every father, mother, teacher and neighbour who has a household in their care. The wicked slave says in his heart, “My master is delayed,” and that thought is the beginning of the fall. Maria had eleven years; she was found faithful. A Ramban's life, whatever its length, is measured by the same question. Let us ask it of ourselves: if the Lord came this evening, what would he find us doing?
outline: Ask: whom do I remember with thanks for the faith that came to me, and what do I imitate in them?
Remembering as a school: consider the outcome of their lives, imitate their faith; the Ramban remembered by name only.
Point 2 · The same yesterday and today
Leaders pass, Christ remains; the altar from which we are fed, where we also remember the dead.
Jesus suffered outside the gate; no lasting city; St Maria Goretti said no and forgave.
Point 4 · At work when the master comes
A sacrifice of praise and of sharing; the faithful and wise servant.
“Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
live: Name three people who handed on the faith to you, among them a priest or monk, and pray for them at the next Holy Qurbono.
Begin and end this day with a short prayer of thanksgiving, “the fruit of lips that confess his name.”
Choose one person who has hurt you and pray for them by name each evening this week.
2027-07-06.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the same yesterday and today and for ever. We thank you for those who spoke your word to us, and we commend to you your servant Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban, whose memory the Church keeps today; reward every priest and monk who served you faithfully. Let us consider the outcome of their lives and imitate their faith. Feed us at your altar, strengthen our hearts with your grace, and teach us to go out to you outside the camp, looking for the city that is to come. Through the prayers of St Maria Goretti, who refused what was wrong and forgave her enemy, make us brave in goodness and gentle in forgiveness. Find us at work, faithful and wise, when you come. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Epistle says, “We have an altar,” and at the Holy Qurbono the Church stands at that altar to be fed with the Body and Blood of the Lord and to remember the faithful departed, including the priests and monks who once stood where the priest stands now.
conn: Hebrews 13:8: “the same yesterday and today and forever”; Malachi 3:6: “For I the Lord do not change”; Hebrews 1:12 says the same of the Son.

Leviticus 16:27 describes the sin offering burned outside the camp; Hebrews 13:11–13 sees Jesus suffer outside the gate; Luke 23:34 gives his prayer for those who crucified him, which Maria Goretti repeated in her own way.
Hosea 14:2 speaks of “the fruit of our lips”; Hebrews 13:15–16 joins praise and sharing; Matthew 24:45–46 names the faithful servant found at work.
fathers: His mother Monica, on her deathbed, asked only this of her sons: lay this body anywhere, and let it not trouble you; only remember me at the altar of the Lord (Confessions 9.11, in substance).

At the holy sacrifice we pray for the holy fathers and bishops who have fallen asleep, and for all who have fallen asleep among us, believing that it is of the greatest benefit to them while the holy and most awesome sacrifice lies before us (Mystagogical Catecheses 5.9, in substance).
magis: The Eucharistic sacrifice is also offered for the faithful departed who have died in Christ but are not yet fully purified, so that they may enter into the light and peace of Christ (in substance).

From the beginning the Church has honoured the memory of the dead and offered prayers for them, above all the Eucharistic sacrifice, so that, purified, they may attain the beatific vision of God (in substance).
Martyrdom is the supreme witness given to the truth of the faith; the martyr bears witness to Christ even to death, and the Church has always honoured such witness (in substance).
term: A title in the Syriac tradition for a monk-priest. It comes from the Syriac word rabban, “our teacher”. In the Malankara tradition it names a priest who has taken the monastic vows of a life of prayer and service.
kidsaint: Maria was a poor girl in Italy who helped her mother in the house and the fields, and who loved to pray. When she was only eleven, someone tried to make her do something wrong. Maria was very brave and said no, because she knew it would hurt God. She was badly hurt for this, and in hospital, before she died, she said that she forgave the person. Today the Church remembers her as a saint, a brave and forgiving friend of Jesus. Lesson: say no to what is wrong, and forgive those who hurt you, as Jesus did.

quick: The Epistle says: remember your leaders, imitate their faith, and know that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
We have an altar from which we are fed; we go out to Jesus outside the camp, looking for the city that is to come; we offer praise and share what we have.
The Gospel asks us to be the faithful and wise servant whom the master finds at work when he comes.
2027-07-06.action: Pray today, by name, for three people who handed on the faith to you, and for one person who has hurt you.
2027-07-06.question: If the Lord came this evening, what would he find me doing?

family.explain: Today the Church remembers Joseph Ramban, a monk-priest, and St Maria Goretti, a brave young girl. The letter tells us to remember the people who taught us about God and to follow their faith. People change, they grow old and they go to God, but Jesus never changes: he is the same yesterday, today and for ever. Jesus also tells us to be good servants who are found doing their work when he comes. Maria was only eleven, but she said no to what was wrong and she forgave someone who hurt her, and God found her ready.
family.intention: We pray for those who taught us the faith, for those who have died, and for children who are in danger or who are hurt.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught you to pray? Let us say thank you to God for them.”

illus: In a church near Changanassery the family of an old priest kept his ormma every year on the same day. The younger grandchildren, who had never known him, asked what he had been like. His niece did not describe his sermons. She said that when the first monsoon rains came he would walk the parish roads with a big black umbrella, stopping at every house where someone was ill, and that he was never once seen to hurry. One of the boys asked what he had said to the sick. She answered that mostly he sat with them, and sometimes he said the Lord's Prayer, and then he went home. At the end of the lunch the boy said that he wanted to be like the umbrella man. His niece told the family later that she had never been so moved by a remark; she believed that was exactly how a memory should work.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the same yesterday, today and for ever, we thank you for those who spoke your word to us. Help us to remember them at your altar, to imitate their faith, and to be found faithful when you come. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you (Hebrews 13:7). Who comes to my mind, and what do I want to imitate in them?
Let us then go to him outside the camp (Hebrews 13:13). What comfort am I asked to leave for the sake of the Lord?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What is the work he has given me in my household?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful and wise.
interc: For the Church, that she may remember her leaders with gratitude and imitate their faith.
For monks, nuns, priests and bishops, living and dead, and in a special way for Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban.
For children and young people, that they may have the courage to say no to what is wrong and to forgive.
For those who have been hurt by others, that God may give them healing and a heart ready to forgive.
For all of us, that when the master comes he may find us at work.
pm.close: Father, you gave us leaders who spoke your word, and you gave us a saint who forgave to the end. Keep us faithful, so that your Son may find us watching when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam keeps in bold the memory of Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban, a monk-priest, and it also remembers St Maria Goretti. The Epistle gives us a rule for such days: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). And it adds at once: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). People pass away, but he does not.

We have an altar, says the Letter (Hebrews 13:10). At the Holy Qurbono we are fed with the Body and Blood of the Lord, and we remember those who have gone before us, among them the priests and monks who once served at the altar. The Letter also says that Jesus suffered outside the city gate, and that we are to go to him outside the camp (Hebrews 13:12–13), for here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come (Hebrews 13:14).

St Maria Goretti did this at the age of eleven. She refused what was wrong, and when she was dying she forgave the one who had hurt her. She prayed, in her own way, what Jesus had prayed: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34). The Gospel tells us to be like the faithful and wise servant, whom the master will find at work when he comes (Matthew 24:46).
So let us remember with thanks those who taught us the faith, let us offer God a sacrifice of praise, let us forgive anyone who has hurt us, and let us be ready. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know who taught you to pray? Perhaps your mother or grandmother or a priest. Today we say thank you to God for them. We also remember Maria Goretti, a girl who was only eleven years old. She was very brave. She said no to something that was wrong, and she forgave a person who had hurt her. Jesus is the same today as he was long ago, and he helps us to be brave and kind too. This evening, say a little prayer of thanks for someone who taught you about Jesus, and forgive anyone who has been unkind to you.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”

On Tuesday of the seventh week after Pentecost, the memory of Pulikkottil Joseph Ramban with St Maria Goretti: remembering our leaders, the altar, the way outside the camp, and the servant found at work.

sub: Remembering as a school of faith.
Consider the outcome of their lives and imitate their faith.
q: Remember the days of old, consider the years long past; ask your father, and he will inform you; your elders, and they will tell you.
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.
points.apply: Pray at the next Holy Qurbono for three people who handed on the faith to you.

sub: We have an altar from which we are fed.
We remember the dead at the altar.
q: For I the Lord do not change; therefore you, O children of Jacob, have not perished.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: When you receive the Holy Qurbono this week, thank God that Christ does not change, and bring one departed person to his altar.

sub: Jesus suffered outside the city gate.
Here we have no lasting city.
St Maria Goretti said no and forgave.
q: I am a stranger and an alien residing among you
For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.
points.apply: Say no this week to something you know to be wrong, and forgive one person who has hurt you.

points.h: At work when the master arrives
sub: A sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
“My master is delayed” is where the fall begins.
q: The faithful will abound with blessings, but one who is in a hurry to be rich will not go unpunished.
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.
points.apply: Do today the work that the Lord has put into your hands, in your household, with praise and with sharing.

concl: The Church remembers her leaders to imitate their faith, and the faith is in the One who does not change.
We are fed at the altar, we go out to him, and we are ready: the master will find us at work.
2027-07-06.resolve: Remember with thanks, forgive from the heart, and be found at work when the Lord comes.
